name: Shackleton Crater Rim (Connecting Ridge)
agency: Artemis III candidate in NASA's 2022 list (Connecting Ridge); not in the Oct 2024 list
description: High-elevation ridge adjacent to Shackleton Crater, famous for 'peaks of eternal light' with over 80% annual solar illumination and prime proximity to permanently shadowed water-ice traps. Note: the Shackleton-de Gerlache Connecting Ridge was one of NASA's 13 Artemis III candidate regions in 2022 but is not among the 9 regions in NASA's October 2024 update.

snap.note: local summit of the connecting ridge

name: Shackleton Crater Floor (PSR)
description: Deep interior floor of Shackleton Crater. A Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) where sunlight never reaches and temperatures stay below 40 K, preserving ancient water ice.

snap.note: deepest point of Shackleton crater floor

name: Malapert Massif Peak
agency: NASA Artemis III candidate region (Oct 2024) / relay candidate
description: 5-km tall mountain peak near the south pole offering nearly uninterrupted Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight communication alongside extended solar power windows.

name: Nobile Western Rim (NASA VIPER Target)
agency: NASA VIPER target area; Artemis III candidate regions nearby (Nobile Rim 1/2, Mons Mouton, Oct 2024)
description: Targeted for lunar rover volatile prospecting; balances gentle slopes for roving with intermittent sunlight and Earth communication windows.

name: Apollo Basin (Chang'e-6 Landing Site)
description: Historic 2024 far-side sample return site. Because it faces away from Earth, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) visibility is 0%, proving why relay satellites like Queqiao-2 are mandatory.

name: Mare Tranquillitatis (Apollo 11)
description: Equatorial baseline site demonstrating standard ~14.7-day lunar daylight cycles, high overhead sun angles, and permanent Earth visibility high in the sky.
